precepts.text: And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls. So that is what it means, we shall inherit them. We shall own and possess them. And their kings shall minister unto thee: for in my wrath I smote thee. Meaning slavery. In God's wrath he smote us, meaning he allowed us to go into slavery. But in my favour have I had mercy on thee. That is Christ dying on the cross and delivering us. Therefore thy gates shall be open continually. So the gates of New Jerusalem shall be opened continually. They shall not be shut day nor night. Why? That men may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles. That men may bring the wealth, the riches of the Gentiles. Why? Because it is ours. It has always been ours. And that their kings may be brought. Brought as what? Slaves. For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish. Any nation that will not serve the Lord shall perish. It starts with Christ first. Understand that he is our king. His orders are our orders. He gives us an order, we carry it out to the nations. Whoever does not obey shall perish. Yea, those nations shall be utterly wasted.
precepts.point: And make the desolate cities to be inhabited. Why do churches never read this kind of stuff? Why do apologists never read this type of stuff?

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

precepts.why:
What does it mean to inherit the Gentiles? “And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls.” That's what it means: we shall own and possess them. “and their kings shall minister unto thee.”

“for in my wrath I smote thee”: that's slavery. In his wrath God smote us, meaning he allowed us to go into slavery. “but in my favour have I had mercy on thee”: that's Christ dying on the cross and delivering us.

“Therefore thy gates shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day nor night.” The gates of New Jerusalem shall be open continually. Why? “that men may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles”: the wealth, the riches of the Gentiles. Why? Because it's ours. It has always been ours. “and that their kings may be brought”: brought as what? Slaves.

“For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish; yea, those nations shall be utterly wasted.” Any nation that will not serve the Lord shall perish. It starts with Christ first. He is our king; his orders are our orders. He gives us an order, and we carry it out to the nations. Whoever does not obey shall perish. That is the seed of Isaiah 54 inheriting the Gentiles and making the desolate cities to be inhabited.

precepts.text: For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth. Covered with what? Sin, lies, deceit. And gross darkness the people. And the people is talking about the twelve tribes. We are in the worst type of darkness. But the Lord shall arise upon thee, and his glory shall be seen upon thee.
precepts.point: And the vail that is spread over all nations.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

precepts.why:
“And he will destroy in this mountain the face of the covering cast over all people, and the vail that is spread over all nations.” He is going to destroy all the lies this white man cast over all people: that God is white, Jesus is white, the angels are white, the Jews are white. Isaiah 60 is a precept for that verse.

“For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth.” Covered with what? Sin, lies and deceit. That darkness is the covering cast over all people and the vail spread over all nations.

“and gross darkness the people.” The people is talking about the twelve tribes. We are in the worst type of darkness, because the lies were cast over us first and deepest.

“but the Lord shall arise upon thee, and his glory shall be seen upon thee.” When the Lord arises upon Israel, the covering is destroyed and his glory is seen on his people. That is the feast in the mountain of Isaiah 25:6: the lies are taken away, the vail is removed, and the people who sat in gross darkness are the ones his glory rests upon.

precepts.text: Violence shall no more be heard in thy land, nor wasting nor destruction within thy borders: no bombs in Tel Aviv, Ashdod or Ashkelon when the rightful people are placed there.
precepts.point: Men shall dwell in it and there shall be no more utter destruction, but Jerusalem shall be safely inhabited: if the people there were the right people there would be no war, because the Messiah must return before we enter the land. That is why they are being blown to hell.

note.label: Edom: The Robbers of thy people revealed past and present

precepts.why:
Zechariah ends the day of the Lord with this: “And men shall dwell in it, and there shall be no more utter destruction; but Jerusalem shall be safely inhabited.” The it is the land. When the Lord returns, men shall dwell in it and there shall be no more destruction. Isaiah says the same: “Violence shall no more be heard in thy land, wasting nor destruction within thy borders”.

That is the time when all Israel, all of us, will be in the land. No bombs in Tel Aviv, no bombs in Ashdod, no bombs in Ashkelon, none of that, once the rightful people are rightfully placed in the land. That is not now. “But thou shalt call thy walls Salvation, and thy gates Praise”, because we will be safe living in them.

So if you are the people of the land, why is the war taking place? The prophecy says there will be no more war and destruction in the land once the Lord returns and we get the land. That means you don't belong there. Prophecy shows the Messiah must return for us to get into the land, not before; that is against prophecy. That is why they are getting blown to hell over there.

What is happening now is the first half of Zechariah 14: all nations gathered against Jerusalem to battle, the city taken, the houses rifled, the women ravished. Jerusalem has become “a burdensome stone for all people”: the Israelis are trying to hold on to this land and expand it, and it is becoming a burdensome stone to them, because they are not the chosen people of God. Only when the Lord's feet stand on the mount of Olives, and he is king over all the earth, is violence no more heard in the land.

precepts.text: Thy people also shall be all righteous and inherit the land for ever: the people over there are not all righteous, so they cannot be the guys.
precepts.point: Men shall dwell in it and there shall be no more utter destruction, but Jerusalem shall be safely inhabited: if the people there were the right people there would be no war, because the Messiah must return before we enter the land. That is why they are being blown to hell.

note.label: Edom: The Robbers of thy people revealed past and present

precepts.why:
Zechariah says that when the Lord is king over all the earth, “Jerusalem shall be safely inhabited.” Isaiah says who will inhabit it: “Thy people also shall be all righteous: they shall inherit the land for ever”.

Are the people over there in Israel today all righteous? No. So they cannot be the guys, because they are not all righteous. That doesn't make any damn sense at all.

Ezekiel confirms it: in the latter years we come “into the land that is brought back from the sword, and is gathered out of many people, against the mountains of Israel, which have been always waste: but it is brought forth out of the nations, and they shall dwell safely all of them.” Is the land still waste today? Yes, it is even worse now. Are the Israelis dwelling safely right now? No. They are in bomb shelters, running and hiding, crying about how unsanitary the shelters are. Where is their God at? On vacation? With Epstein? With Bibi? Where is the great Hashem at?

The righteous people who inherit the land for ever are the ones brought forth out of the nations, gathered by the Lord when he returns. That is why Joel says he pleads “for my people and for my heritage Israel”: my people and my land, not all people. He is coming to save his people and give the land to his people, and they shall be all righteous.

precepts.point: The whirlwind of the Lord goeth forth with fury and falls upon the head of the wicked, and the fierce anger of the Lord shall not return until he hath performed the intents of his heart; in the latter days ye shall consider it.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
“the city shall be builded upon her own heap, and the palace shall remain after the manner thereof.” It says heap because that land is going to be destroyed and built again; the palace means the temple that is going to be built. Isaiah 60 goes with Jeremiah 30:18.

“And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls, and their kings shall minister unto thee: for in my wrath I smote thee, but in my favour have I had mercy on thee.” The strangers build the walls when Jerusalem is built again on her own heap.

“The glory of Lebanon shall come unto thee, the fir tree, the pine tree, and the box together, to beautify the place of my sanctuary”. That is the palace. “and I will make the place of my feet glorious”: the Lord is going to make Jerusalem glorious again.

precepts.point: The whirlwind of the Lord goeth forth with fury and falls upon the head of the wicked, and the fierce anger of the Lord shall not return until he hath performed the intents of his heart; in the latter days ye shall consider it.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
Jeremiah says, “I will multiply them, and they shall not be few; I will also glorify them, and they shall not be small.” That is why we go to Isaiah 60.

“Thy people also shall be all righteous: they shall inherit the land for ever, the branch of my planting, the work of my hands, that I may be glorified.” Then: “A little one shall become a thousand, and a small one a strong nation: I the Lord will hasten it in his time.” We shall not be small.

There is more in that verse than what it is saying on the surface. Look at the little bodies we have now. We are not going to have these little bodies. We are not going to be all frail and skinny, and the little fat brothers are not going to be like that either. The Lord multiplies and glorifies Israel, in number and in body.

precepts.text: Of the children of the strangers that sojourn among you shall ye buy, and they shall be your possession and your bondmen for ever; but over your brethren ye shall not rule with rigour. That is the law behind the strangers building the walls.
precepts.point: The glory of Lebanon, the fir, pine, and box, shall beautify the place of my sanctuary; Lebanon and its famous trees belong to the Israelites. The sons of them that afflicted thee shall come bending, and all that despised thee shall bow at the soles of thy feet and call thee the city of the Lord, the Zion of the Holy One of Israel. That is what Revelation 3:9 said. The third temple is under Christ, not under Edom.

note.label: Prophesy From Pain to Peace

precepts.why:
Isaiah 60 is the true third temple. Solomon built the first; Zerubbabel and Joshua rebuilt the second during the Persian captivity; and here is the third. “And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls”. The third temple is built by the other nations, because the other nations will be our slaves. That makes some nervous, but that is what it says.

Here is the law behind it, for anyone struggling: “Moreover of the children of the strangers that do sojourn among you, of them shall ye buy, and of their families that are with you, which they begat in your land: and they shall be your possession.” Those are the same strangers Isaiah speaks of in verse 10. We shall own them, possess them as slaves.

“And ye shall take them as an inheritance for your children after you, to inherit them for a possession; they shall be your bondmen for ever”. For how long? For ever. Then: “but over your brethren the children of Israel, ye shall not rule one over another with rigour”.

So when Isaiah says “their kings shall minister unto thee”, it is that law being carried out in the kingdom. God was angry with us and smote us, and we went into slavery: “in my wrath I smote thee”. Then: “but in my favour have I had mercy on thee”: that is why he sent Christ. Now the order is turned back to what the law always said: the strangers serve, and Israel is not ruled with rigour.

The people shall bring them to their place: the Arabs out of North Africa, which is Ham's, the white man out of Australia and South Africa. Israel shall possess them for servants and handmaids, take them captives whose captives they were, and rule over their oppressors, and the Lord shall give thee rest from thy sorrow and from the hard bondage. note.label: Prophesy From Pain to Peace

precepts.why:
What about the strangers? Are they going to be in the kingdom? Yes, but read how. “For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land”. He is not having mercy on everybody on the planet. He said Jacob: the twelve tribes of Israel. That's us. He will set them in their own land: not the League of Nations, not the UN.

Then: “and the strangers shall be joined with them, and they shall cleave to the house of Jacob”: joined to obey us. “And the people shall take them, and bring them to their place”. All nations will be put where they rightfully belong. The Arabs in North Africa are not supposed to be there; that belongs to Ham, and they will be moved out. The white man in Australia does not belong there, and the white man in South Africa will be removed out of that land.

Then: “and the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord for servants and handmaids: and they shall take them captives, whose captives they were; and they shall rule over their oppressors”. That is the law of Leviticus 25 just read: the laws will be re-implemented.

“And it shall come to pass in the day that the Lord shall give thee rest from thy sorrow, and from thy fear, and from the hard bondage wherein thou wast made to serve”. That is why Christ said come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. People say rest from sin; not just sin. Slavery is the result of sin, and oppression is the result of sin. That is the rest Christ was talking about.

Back in Isaiah 60, that is why “the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls”: we will possess them, as servants and handmaids. The Bible does not contradict itself; Christianity contradicts the Bible.

note.label: Prophesy From Pain to Peace

precepts.why:
Still on the third temple: “And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them”. Power was given unto them.

Then: “and I saw the souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God”: the martyred. Then: “and which had not worshipped the beast, neither his image, neither had received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands”: the mark of sin, that lets you know it is somebody in these last days, who would not support the beast.

Then: “and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years”. Notice the top of it: thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them. This is the third temple being built up. We are going to reign with Christ for a thousand years.

That is why Isaiah 60 ends with the ones who afflicted us bowing: “all they that despised thee shall bow themselves down at the soles of thy feet; and they shall call thee, The city of the Lord, The Zion of the Holy One of Israel.” It is the same thing Revelation 3:9 said. The third temple is under Christ, not what the Christians make of Daniel 9.

note.label: Prophesy From Pain to Peace

precepts.why:
“And the nations of them which are saved shall walk in the light of it: and the kings of the earth do bring their glory and honour into it.” Saved here does not mean what people get confused about. It means left over: “every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem”. Those that are left walk in the light of it: they obey the commandments, and come up to worship the King of kings and keep the feast of tabernacles.

“And the gates of it shall not be shut at all by day: for there shall be no night there.” That is the third temple, the same gates of Isaiah 60: “thy gates shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day nor night; that men may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles, and that their kings may be brought.” Forces means wealth, and their kings are brought in chains. “For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish”.

“And they shall bring the glory and honour of the nations into it. And there shall in no wise enter into it any thing that defileth, neither whatsoever worketh abomination, or maketh a lie: but they which are written in the Lamb’s book of life.” So the nations themselves are not walking in. They are bringing their glory and honour up to the men of God at the gates. Those written in the Lamb's book of life are the Israelites. Only the Israelites get in.

note.label: Prophesy From Pain to Peace

precepts.why:
When Revelation says “the nations of them which are saved”, Zechariah gives the thought: “And it shall come to pass, that every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem shall even go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles.”

Everyone that is left. Christ is not killing everybody. There are going to be remnants of people left over from the nations that came against Jerusalem. Those are the “saved” of Revelation 21: the ones left.

And what they do is go up every year to worship the King and keep the feast of tabernacles. That is walking in the light of it: obeying the commandments. That is how the nations serve in Isaiah 60, bringing their wealth and their kings to the gates while Israel is inside. “For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish; yea, those nations shall be utterly wasted.”

note.label: Prophesy From Pain to Peace

precepts.why:
If they want to use any scripture about a third temple, this is where you go. If they build that temple, this is what we are going to use: “Who opposeth and exalteth himself above all that is called God, or that is worshipped; so that he as God sitteth in the temple of God, shewing himself that he is God.”

Who is that? The white man, who opposes everything the Bible says. Before 70 AD, before they destroyed it, Rome entered our temple and sat their rusty butt down. And after Titus destroyed Jerusalem, Rome built Aelia Capitolina on its ruins, named for the emperor Hadrian, whose clan name was Aelius, and for Jupiter, Juno and Minerva: that is the trinity, where Christianity got that doctrine. A sanctuary to Jupiter, that is Zeus, the devil, was built on the Temple Mount, statues of Roman gods were set up in intentional violation of Old Testament law, and the real Jews were forbidden the city. The walls of the old city today follow the Roman walls: the wailing wall they hump on nowadays.

Now they are trying to build on the Temple Mount again. If the Lord allows them to be successful, one will sit there saying I am God, and everybody will cheer. No. That is the man Paul warned of.

The true third temple is the one in Isaiah 60, under Christ: the strangers build its walls, the nations bring their wealth to its gates, and those who despised us bow at the soles of our feet and call it “The city of the Lord, The Zion of the Holy One of Israel.”

precepts.text: Arise, shine, for thy light is come: awake to righteousness and go teach. Darkness shall cover the earth, the nations defiled by Edom, and gross darkness the people, God's people, affected by it. But the Lord shall arise upon thee, on those who want to stop sinning, not those taking advantage of his mercy.
precepts.point: I will bring plagues upon the world, the sword, famine, death, and destruction, for wickedness hath exceedingly polluted the whole earth and their hurtful works are fulfilled. Esau did that: Malachi calls Edom the border of wickedness, and 1 Maccabees 1:9 says after Alexander's death evils were multiplied in the earth, from the Greeks through Rome, Spain, France, Germany, Britain, Russia, and America.

note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.why:
The earth is under much wickedness, in gross darkness. Isaiah says, “Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee.” Arise: awake to righteousness; it is time to wake up out of that deep sleep. Shine: that is going out to teach, letting your light shine, teaching God's commandments. Our light is Christ.

“For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the people”. The darkness covering the earth is the nations: every nation is affected by the United States of America, by Edom, and the whole world is defiled because of this nation. And because of that, the Israelites have been affected: gross darkness the people, God's people.

Then: “but the Lord shall arise upon thee, and his glory shall be seen upon thee.” The Lord is still going to arise upon us, because he is still going to choose Israel and have mercy on his people: the ones who want to stop sinning, not the ones who take advantage of God's grace and mercy. His glory shall be seen upon his people.

precepts.text: Thy people also shall be all righteous; they shall inherit the land for ever. A little one shall become a thousand: the Lord will bring certain spirits back quickly through marriage and childbearing.
precepts.point: At destruction and famine thou shalt laugh, the beasts of the field shall be at peace with thee, thy tabernacle shall be in peace, and thou shalt not sin: Isaiah 60:21 says thy people shall be all righteous. Thy seed shall be great as the grass, and thou shalt come to thy grave in a full age like a shock of corn in its season: Israel's life will be long, forever.

note.label: Edom's Achilles' Heel

precepts.why:
Job 5:24: “And thou shalt know that thy tabernacle shall be in peace; and thou shalt visit thy habitation, and shalt not sin.” We won’t sin. Isaiah 60:21 says the same.

“Thy people also shall be all righteous”: our people shall be all righteous. “They shall inherit the land for ever”: we shall inherit the land forever. “The branch of my planting, the work of my hands, that I may be glorified”: we are the branch of God’s planting.

“A little one shall become a thousand, and a small one a strong nation: I the Lord will hasten it in his time.” We are going to have a whole lot of children. He is going to make sure to bring back certain spirits through marriage and childbearing; certain spirits are going to come back real quick.

That is Job 5:25-26: “thy seed shall be great, and thine offspring as the grass of the earth.” Our children are going to grow up quick. “Thou shalt come to thy grave in a full age, like as a shock of corn cometh in in his season.” Like a shock of corn comes back over and over, Israel is going to have a long, long life. That is why he calls it forever, eternal.

precepts.text: Darkness covers the earth and gross darkness the people until Israel's light comes.
precepts.point: The moon is an instrument of the armies above.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
“Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee.” Arise means wake up; shine means teach; and the light that is come is Christ, who said, I am the light. “For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the people”. We are in the grossest of darkness; we have lost our heritage and lost everything. When you see the moon dark, that is what it represents: darkness has covered the whole world.

Psalms 82 shows the same darkness. “God standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods.” The little g is us. Asaph, with the Holy Spirit upon him, records what we did wrong as the gods of the earth: “How long will ye judge unjustly, and accept the persons of the wicked?” We were to defend the poor and fatherless and deliver the needy, but “they walk on in darkness: all the foundations of the earth are out of course.” “I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.” “But ye shall die like men”: our godhood was taken from us. “Arise, O God, judge the earth: for thou shalt inherit all nations.”

Something in the heavens is out of course because of our sins. God made “two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night”. But in the kingdom, Isaiah 30:26: “Moreover the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, as the light of seven days, in the day that the Lord bindeth up the breach of his people, and healeth the stroke of their wound.” The sun has no phases; in the kingdom the moon, the sign of the world, will not go dark again. And the sun we call so bright is not bright at all next to that.

Binding up the breach is Amos 9:11: “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof”, gathering the twelve tribes of Israel back again. That is when Isaiah 60:1 is fulfilled: our light is come, the moon is back at its fullness, and Israel is back in the kingdom.

precepts.text: The nation that will not serve Israel shall perish.
precepts.point: The residue of men seek after the Lord in servitude, and the Gentiles called by his name are those who call themselves Jews and Christians.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
Simeon's words, “That the residue of men might seek after the Lord”, can be confusing. How are they going to seek after the Lord? Isaiah answers it: “For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish; yea, those nations shall be utterly wasted.”

They will seek after the Lord in captivity. There is no we're equal to you, we're ruling with you. The nations don't get a pass for all the evil they did. They are going to learn God's laws, his statutes and his commandments, and they will learn them in slavery, serving Israel. Whoever does not want to follow it shall be put to death. That is what the Bible says.

precepts.text: The city needs no sun or moon, for the Lamb is the light thereof.
precepts.point: Only those written in the Lamb's book of life enter, the twelve tribes of Israel.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
“The sun shall be no more thy light by day; neither for brightness shall the moon give light unto thee: but the Lord shall be unto thee an everlasting light, and thy God thy glory.” That does not mean there will be no sun and no moon. They will always be there. But we are not going to need that light, because we are going to be on another level: a spiritual level, a god level.

Revelation shows the same thing: “And the city had no need of the sun, neither of the moon, to shine in it: for the glory of God did lighten it, and the Lamb is the light thereof.” That is what we just read in Isaiah 60:19.

The city is “the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.” That is what Christ meant when he said, Thy kingdom come. It “had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel.”

“Thy sun shall no more go down; neither shall thy moon withdraw itself: for the Lord shall be thine everlasting light, and the days of thy mourning shall be ended.” Everything goes back to the way it was. Israel in the kingdom lives in the light of the Lamb, and the days of our mourning are ended.

precepts.text: The kings of the earth bring their glory and honour into it.
precepts.point: Only those written in the Lamb's book of life enter, the twelve tribes of Israel.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
“And the nations of them which are saved shall walk in the light of it: and the kings of the earth do bring their glory and honour into it.” People use this to say all the nations will be saved. But saved does not mean salvation here; it is in the context of rulership. Saved from what?

The precept is Zechariah: “And it shall come to pass, that every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem shall even go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles.” Saved means left: they were left from being destroyed. Christ did not destroy them, and they are going to obey. Walking in the light of it means they serve the King and keep the feast of tabernacles.

“and the kings of the earth do bring their glory and honour into it”, as Isaiah says: “Therefore thy gates shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day nor night; that men may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles, and that their kings may be brought.”

“And there shall in no wise enter into it any thing that defileth, neither whatsoever worketh abomination, or maketh a lie: but they which are written in the Lamb’s book of life.” Those nations do not walk in. They bring it to us at the front gate, and then they go back. Those written in the Lamb’s book of life are the twelve tribes of Israel.

precepts.text: The Gentiles shall come to thy light.
precepts.point: Only those written in the Lamb's book of life enter, the twelve tribes of Israel.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
“Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee.” God is saying to us, Arise, wake up. Shine means teach. Thy light is come: Christ is come. The glory of the Lord risen upon thee is the Holy Spirit.

“For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the people.” We are in the worst darkness. “but the Lord shall arise upon thee, and his glory shall be seen upon thee”: wisdom and knowledge shall be seen upon us.

“And the Gentiles shall come to thy light, and kings to the brightness of thy rising.” The other nations shall come to our light. What is our light? The laws in Christ. And what does it look like for them to come to it? Zechariah 14: “every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem shall even go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles.” Keeping the high holy days: that is them coming to our light.

That is why the Lord is our everlasting light in Isaiah 60:19. The nations do not bring the light; they come to Israel’s light and bring their kings and their wealth to it.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
“And it shall come to pass, that from one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another, shall all flesh come to worship before me, saith the Lord.” This was brought up for the nations coming to Israel’s light in the kingdom.

The book, chapter and verse the Bishop was looking for is Zechariah 14, where it is spelled out: “every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem shall even go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles.” The nations that are left come up to worship at the appointed times, keeping the high holy days. That is them coming to our light.

So all flesh coming to worship is not all flesh entering the city. They are the nations left from destruction, serving and worshipping the King at his feasts, while only those written in the Lamb’s book of life, the twelve tribes of Israel, enter the city whose everlasting light is the Lord.

precepts.text: Thy people shall be all righteous; they shall inherit the land for ever.
precepts.point: Violence shall no more be heard in the land, and the people shall be all righteous.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
Peter says “we, according to his promise, look for new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness.” Isaiah 60 shows what that promise is. “Violence shall no more be heard in thy land”: the white man will be subdued, because he is the violent man, behind every coup and every war. The land is the land of Israel, with no “wasting nor destruction within thy borders”, and “thou shalt call thy walls Salvation, and thy gates Praise.”

“The sun shall be no more thy light by day; neither for brightness shall the moon give light unto thee: but the Lord shall be unto thee an everlasting light”. That doesn't mean the sun and moon are done away with; they will be there, but the Israelites won't need them, because the Lord will be our light. “Thy sun shall no more go down”: our understanding shall no more go down, and our moon, our understanding, won't withdraw itself. And “the days of thy mourning shall be ended.”

“Thy people also shall be all righteous: they shall inherit the land for ever”. That is why the new earth is one wherein dwelleth righteousness: because our people shall be all righteous. Esau isn't going to be there enjoying anything. “A little one shall become a thousand, and a small one a strong nation”: we're going to have a whole lot of children. “I the Lord will hasten it in his time”: I'm going to speed it up.

The scoffers say all things continue as they were. But one day is with the Lord as a thousand years; he is not slack concerning his promise. So, beloved, seeing we look for such things, be diligent to be found of him in peace, without sin, and blameless.

precepts.text: Future prophecy: the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls and their kings minister unto thee, and the nation that will not serve thee shall perish.
precepts.point: This type of ordeal will play out again in the times when Christ returns: the sons of strangers shall come to build up Israel's walls, their kings shall minister unto Israel, and the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish. There is nothing new under the sun.

note.label: Joshua 9: The Gibeonite Deception and the Weight of an Oath

precepts.why:
Joshua made peace with the Gibeonites and “made a league with them, to let them live”, and the princes sware unto them. This type of ordeal will play out again in the times when Christ returns; there is nothing new under the sun.

“And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls, and their kings shall minister unto thee: for in my wrath I smote thee, but in my favour have I had mercy on thee.” Israel’s gates shall be open continually, “that men may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles, and that their kings may be brought.” And “the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish; yea, those nations shall be utterly wasted.” Strangers left alive to serve Israel, as the Gibeonites were, is future prophecy as well as history.

precepts.text: The nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish; the sons of them that afflicted thee shall come bending unto thee; it shall happen again.
precepts.point: When Christ returns he will destroy all nations in the valley of Megiddo, and after Israel's spirits are changed he will thrust out the enemy from before us and say, Destroy them. Israel will lay the vengeance of the Most High upon Edom according to his anger and according to his fury. Brothers, you just have to endure to the end; this is how you read the Bible, precept upon precept, here a little and there a little.

note.label: Joshua 11: The Northern Kings Utterly Destroyed

precepts.why:
“There was not a city that made peace with the children of Israel, save the Hivites the inhabitants of Gibeon”; that is why all of them went into destruction. There is nothing new under the sun; it shall happen again, and we are just waiting on it to unfold. “For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish; yea, those nations shall be utterly wasted.”

“The sons also of them that afflicted thee shall come bending unto thee; and all they that despised thee shall bow themselves down at the soles of thy feet; and they shall call thee, The city of the Lord, The Zion of the Holy One of Israel. Whereas thou hast been forsaken and hated, so that no man went through thee, I will make thee an eternal excellency, a joy of many generations.” The nation that will not serve Israel shall perish, as those kings did that would not make peace; and the sons of them that afflicted us shall come bending unto us.

precepts.text: The abundance of the nations and their wealth shall be brought and turned unto restored Israel.
precepts.point: The king and his counselors freely offered silver and gold for the house of God, for sacrifices, and for whatever else was needful, drawn even from the king's treasure house. This was favor, letting the captivity return with the treasures of Babylon, as the nations will one day bring back all Israel's substance.

note.label: Ezra 7: Ezra The Ready Scribe Prepares His Heart

precepts.why:
Artaxerxes and his counsellors freely offered silver and gold “unto the God of Israel, whose habitation is in Jerusalem”, and told Ezra to carry all the silver and gold he could find in the province of Babylon, and to bestow whatever more was needful “out of the king’s treasure house.” That was favor: the captivity going home with the treasures of Babylon.

It is a picture of what the nations will one day do for all Israel. “Then thou shalt see, and flow together, and thine heart shall fear, and be enlarged; because the abundance of the sea shall be converted unto thee, the forces of the Gentiles shall come unto thee. The multitude of camels shall cover thee, the dromedaries of Midian and Ephah; all they from Sheba shall come: they shall bring gold and incense; and they shall shew forth the praises of the Lord.”

The abundance of the nations and their wealth shall be brought and turned unto restored Israel. Ezra carrying the king's silver and gold up to Jerusalem is a foretaste of the nations bringing back all of Israel's substance.

precepts.text: The sons of them that afflicted us shall come bending, showing the strangers submitting themselves.
precepts.point: The Most High delivers him from the strivings of the people and makes him the head of the heathen; a people whom he has not known shall serve him.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

precepts.why:
“As soon as they hear of me, they shall obey me: the strangers shall submit themselves unto me.” Isaiah shows that submission: “The sons also of them that afflicted thee shall come bending unto thee; and all they that despised thee shall bow themselves down at the soles of thy feet”.

The sons of them that afflicted us come bending, and they that despised us bow down at the soles of our feet. That is the strangers submitting themselves, when the Most High makes us the head of the heathen and a people we have not known serve us.

“and they shall call thee, The city of the Lord, The Zion of the Holy One of Israel.” The strangers that fade away and are afraid out of their close places are the very ones who will call us the city of the Lord.

precepts.text: The sons of strangers shall build up thy walls and their kings minister unto thee; the nation that will not serve thee shall perish and be utterly wasted, and they that afflicted thee shall come bending and bow at the soles of thy feet.
precepts.point: The Most High chooses Israel's inheritance for them; it will not be up to you to say you do not want to rule the nations. The spirit will be put on you and you will be kings, your wives goddesses and queens, your sons princes, your daughters princesses, ruling the whole planet in righteousness.

note.label: Psalm 47: God the Great King Over All the Earth

precepts.why:
“He shall subdue the people under us, and the nations under our feet.” Isaiah describes it: “the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls, and their kings shall minister unto thee: for in my wrath I smote thee, but in my favour have I had mercy on thee.” “For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish; yea, those nations shall be utterly wasted.” “The sons also of them that afflicted thee shall come bending unto thee; and all they that despised thee shall bow themselves down at the soles of thy feet; and they shall call thee, The city of the Lord, The Zion of the Holy One of Israel.”

In his wrath he smote us, and in his favour he has mercy on us: the same people once smitten have kings minister to them, and the sons of them that afflicted us come bending and bow at the soles of our feet. Every nation that will not serve us perishes.

That is why “the Lord most high is terrible”, not in an ugly or scary sense but in a powerful sense, like the angel whose countenance was very terrible when he appeared to Samson's mother, going into the power of the angels. Daniel saw the Ancient of Days, the Most High, seated with hair like pure wool, an afro, his throne like fiery flame, a fiery stream before him and millions of angels ministering unto him. That terrible glory is what David means, and that terrible King is the one who puts the nations under our feet.

precepts.point: Israel takes no wood out of the field because they burn the weapons for fuel, and they spoil those that spoiled them and rob those that robbed them. It is a turning: those who took from us, we take from them.

note.label: Ezekiel 39: The Fall of Gog and the Gathering of Israel

precepts.why:
“they shall spoil those that spoiled them, and rob those that robbed them”. Isaiah shows the same turning: “thy gates shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day nor night; that men may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles, and that their kings may be brought.”

Israel's gates stand open continually so the forces and wealth of the Gentiles may be brought in, and their kings serve as servants. The mighty men who came up against Israel have their shields, bows, arrows, handstaves and spears burned for fuel seven years; beaten into submission, they work the land instead of making war.

Those who took from us, we take from them. Their weapons become our firewood and their wealth comes in through our open gates.

precepts.text: The sons of strangers will build up the walls and their kings will minister, so the other nations build the temple while Israel's working days are over.
precepts.point: It has a wall round about, five hundred reeds long and five hundred broad, to make a separation between the sanctuary and the profane place. By rehearsing these measurements in such detail, the vision is pointing to the kingdom: the temple will be established again with the same measurements given to King Solomon, done all over again. As for why the Father requires such careful preparation, that is above our pay grade; we are to follow and learn, for His thoughts are not our thoughts.

note.label: Ezekiel 42: The Priests' Chambers and the Separation of the Sanctuary

The measurements in such detail point to the kingdom, when the temple is established again with the same measurements given to King Solomon. The other nations build it, and their kings minister; Israel's working days are over. In His wrath He smote us, but in His favour He has mercy on us.

precepts.why: Rank in the kingdom: “I will also make thy officers peace, and thine exactors righteousness.” That goes right back to Deuteronomy 16:18 and Isaiah 1. Don’t ever think there will be no rank in the kingdom and we are all equal; there must be order. Without order you have chaos.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 15 The Seven Last Plagues

precepts.why: “For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish.” “And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls, and their kings shall minister unto thee”: they are going to be our slaves. “For in my wrath I smote thee”: he made us slaves. “But in my favour have I had mercy on thee”: he is going to set us on top as the top nation on earth. “That men may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles”: the wealth of the nations. “The sons also of them that afflicted thee shall come bending unto thee”: Esau loves to ask, do you think it’s right that the children pay for the sins of the fathers? Yes, because there is such a thing as regeneration; you are your fathers come back. “Thou shalt also suck the milk of the Gentiles”: everything the Gentiles got belongs to us. “For brass I will bring gold, and for iron I will bring silver.” “I will also make thy officers peace, and thine exactors righteousness”: thine exactors, your tax collectors. precepts.why: “Thy sun shall no more go down; neither shall thy moon withdraw itself: for the Lord shall be thine everlasting light”: that is our understanding. We are not going to lose our understanding ever again.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 21 Thy Kingdom Come

Camels, dromedaries, gold and incense come. “And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls”: this is why I waited, because when it talked about the kingdom descending from heaven, it’s just saying that’s how beautiful it’s going to look. “For in my wrath I smote thee”: slavery, colonialism. “But in my favour have I had mercy on thee”: Christ dying on the cross for us. “Therefore thy gates shall be open continually”: so Isaiah 60:11 goes with Revelation 21:24-25 combined. “The nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish”: when we send our men out to gather the kings of the nations and a nation don’t want to come and bring their wealth, they shall be utterly wasted, and we’re going to drag their kings to the kingdom. We’re going to be filthy rich, the top nation. “A little one shall become a thousand”: that’s how many kids we’re going to have. “I the Lord will hasten it in his time”: that’s why seven women shall take hold of one man; women are going to outnumber men once again.

precepts.why:
I will make them to come and worship before thy feet. Did Christ just make that up? In church you go, not my Jesus. Yes: Christ is going to make sure every prophecy is fulfilled. You don't like the Old Testament because you don't like the prophecies, but when Christ references the prophecies you are confused and don't understand why Jesus would say that, because you have the wrong Jesus in your head.
